continuous_relative_calibration_descript: Makes the calibration relative to the reference device (typically your headset) so that it updates every frame without needing to recalibrate. This REQUIRES Continuous Calibration.

base_stations_power_mgmt_on_shutdown: Turn off Base Stations on SteamVR shutdown
base_stations_power_mgmt_on_shutdown_des: Powered Base Stations are powered down when SteamVR is not in use.
base_stations_power_mgmt_standby_descrip: Base Stations will power off only their lasers for a faster wake up when SteamVR starts. This is unavailable on Base Station 1.0 models and some Base Station 2.0 models, and sleep will be used in these cases.
base_stations_power_mgmt_sleep_descripti: Base Stations will power off their lasers and motors.
base_stations_power_mgmt_warning: * NOT RECOMMENDED for shared tracking spaces with multiple SteamVR users.
settings_advanced_description: Shows extra settings and fine-tuning controls for power users.
settings_calibrate_motion_vectors_descri: Improves movement prediction for more responsive tracking. May affect physics-heavy games.
settings_autofix_playspace_jumps_descrip: Attempts to automatically detect and correct sudden jumps in playspace tracking.
settings_enforce_minimum_rotation_varian: Automatically rejects samples that are rotationally similar to improve calibration quality.
settings_reset_description: Resets all settings to default. This is permanent and cannot be undone.
settings_reset_confirm: This change is permanent and cannot be undone. Are you sure you want to continue?

learn_card_standard_calibration_descript: Learn how to calibrate a pair of devices.
learn_card_continuous_calibration_descri: Calibrate frequently to counteract drift mid-session.
learn_card_base_station_management_descr: Wirelessly control your SteamVR Base Stations.
learn_card_ui_tour_description: An overview of the Space Calibrator interface.
learn_page_standard_desc: Standard Calibration aligns two tracking systems together so that your VR devices work together in the same physical playspace.
learn_page_standard_select_devices_desc: Before starting, the app needs to know which two devices you want to align.
learn_page_standard_ref_device: Reference Device: This device is what you're calibrating to, usually a controller.
learn_page_standard_target_device: Target Device: The unaligned device you're calibrating with, typically a tracker or similar.
learn_page_standard_perform_step1: Hold both devices together firmly in one hand. Hold them as tight as you can so that they do not move during the calibration process.
learn_page_standard_perform_step2: Click on the Standard Calibration button to begin calibrating.
learn_page_standard_perform_step3: Move around your room while moving your devices in a figure eight, as illustrated below.
learn_page_standard_speeds_desc: You can optionally alter the calibration speed to affect how much movement is required. More movement tends to improve calibration quality.
learn_page_standard_speed_fast: Fast: Takes less time to calibrate, but may result in poorer quality calibrations.
learn_page_standard_speed_slow: Slow / Very Slow: Takes longer to calibrate, and tends to yield more accurate calibrations.
learn_page_standard_completion_note: Once the progress bar fills up, your devices should instantly line up in VR. If this doesn't happen, try calibrating again.
learn_page_standard_drift_desc: Over time, your devices may drift, breaking the calibration. If this happens, you will have to re-calibrate to correct it. If you have to do this frequently, you should consider using Continuous Calibration.
learn_page_continuous_desc1: If you notice your devices slowly shifting, rotating, or drifting out of place while playing, Continuous Calibration is a solution to these issues.
learn_page_continuous_desc2: Instead of forcing you to stop and manually calibrate every so often, Continuous Calibration automatically keeps your tracking synced in the background while you play.
learn_page_continuous_note_desc: A dedicated tracker mounted on your headset IS required to use this feature.
learn_page_continuous_desc3: Continuous Calibration attempts to re-calibrate your devices frequently to eliminate any and all drift. It tends to make calibration something you never think about once it's set up.
learn_page_continuous_setup_instructions: To set up Continuous Calibration, first select your devices as explained in the Standard Calibration page. You will want your headset selected as the reference device, and the calibration tracker as the target device. Then click the Continuous Calibration button to start calibrating. It may take a bit of time until the initial calibration is completed, so move around to let the app learn about your tracking!
learn_page_continuous_should_use_standar: Use Standard Calibration if you do not have an extra tracker to mount on your headset, do not spend long sessions in VR, or don't mind re-calibrating every so often whenever drift happens.
learn_page_continuous_should_use_continu: Use Continuous Calibration if you want to practically never think about drift again. This is recommended if you spend a lot of time in VR or notice significant amounts of drift over time.
learn_page_continuous_physical_setup_tit: Physical setup (mounting the tracker onto your headset)
learn_page_continuous_physical_setup_des: To use Continuous Calibration you will need a dedicated tracker attached onto your VR headset. There are various mounts depending on which specific VR headset and tracker you are using. You can typically find 3D models on the internet you can print to get started with, or you can ask around in the community to see what other people did.
Once mounted, the tracker should be securely attached to the headset. It should not wobble, swivel, or shake. The better the mounting the more consistent calibrations should be.
learn_page_basestation_desc: Space Calibrator allows you to control SteamVR Base Stations if you have a compatible BLE Bluetooth adapter available.
learn_page_basestation_1_desc: You can only turn these on or off. Setting channels wirelessly is unsupported, and you will have to press the physical button on the back of the Base Station to alternate between channels.
learn_page_basestation_2_desc1: Manufactured by both Valve and HTC, these have better support for wireless management than 1.0 Base Stations. With these you're able to turn them on and off, and also set their channel. 2.0 Base Stations must each be on a unique channel, otherwise they will not work. Space Calibrator will offer to help you fix this if it happens.
learn_page_basestation_2_desc2: To change the channel of a 2.0 Base Station, navigate to the Base Station Management tab, select the edit button for the Base Station you wish to control, and click on the desired channel (marked in green).
learn_page_basestation_auto_power_desc: You can go to the Settings tab to enable automatic Base Station Management, which will turn on your Base Stations when Space Calibrator is started, and turn them off when you close SteamVR (with Space Calibrator running). Note that manually closing Space Calibrator before closing SteamVR will NOT turn off any Base Stations automatically.
learn_page_ui_tour_desc: This interface is divided into several tabs, each containing various things.
learn_page_ui_tour_cal_desc1: The Calibration tab contains controls relating to calibrations. You control your calibrations here.
learn_page_ui_tour_cal_desc2: At the top, you will see a card showing you whether you have a calibration active, and if so, which type.
learn_page_ui_tour_cal_desc3: Below that, you can select what devices to calibrate with. First, you should select the tracking systems you wish to calibrate. Then, on the left pane you should select what you're going to calibrate with. And on the right pane you should select what you're going to calibrate.
learn_page_ui_tour_cal_desc4: Below that are the buttons to perform a calibration. If you are unsure which calibration you should do, please read the pages talking about Standard and Continuous Calibration to learn more.
learn_page_ui_tour_cal_desc5: At the bottom of the Calibration tab you will find several options to control the calibration. A number of these settings require advanced settings to be visible.
learn_page_ui_tour_bs_desc: Here you can control any Base Stations in your room with a supported BLE Bluetooth adapter. You should typically not have to touch this beyond initial setup.
learn_page_ui_tour_settings_desc1: Here you may set some global settings for the program. These include advanced settings, Base Station Management, and UI language.
learn_page_ui_tour_settings_desc2: Some features in this app require Advanced Settings to be enabled. You should only enable this if you know what you're doing.
guard_description: Records every device's raw poses so a tracking glitch can be analysed afterwards, and keeps a single glitching tracker from moving the whole playspace (fork feature, see docs/DESIGN.md).
guard_recorder_enabled_desc: Keeps a rolling window of every device's raw poses on disk (about 12 MB per minute for ten devices). A marker saves the window around it into an event folder.
guard_record_other_desc: Records only the calibration's two tracking systems by default (the headset with its controllers, and every lighthouse tracker, controller and base station). On: Standable's virtual trackers, Virtual Desktop hand tracking and other systems are recorded too.
guard_keep_stored_on_start: Keep the stored calibration on start
guard_keep_stored_on_start_desc: The first continuous solve after the overlay starts has to pass the normal checks instead of being forced. Keeps a restart of this window from shifting the calibration.
guard_head_mount: Remember where the head tracker sits on the headset
guard_head_mount_desc: Learned while everything tracks well and kept between sessions. At every start the calibration is set from it as soon as you hold still, and solves that would move the tracker on the headset are ignored (five in a row at the same new place count as a re-mount).
guard_head_mount_known: Head tracker on the headset: right {0:.1f} / up {1:.1f} / back {2:.1f} cm ({3:.0f} min learned)
guard_head_mount_learning: Head tracker on the headset: learning ({0:.1f} of 2 min)
guard_head_mount_fix: Slide the calibration back to it
guard_head_mount_fix_desc: When the head tracker has sat more than 2.5 cm from its place on the headset for five seconds while you move slowly, the calibration slides back at 1.5 cm/s. After the head tracker jumps on its own it waits 20 s, and an offset that is still changing is left alone, so a glitching tracker can't take your body along.
guard_head_mount_fixing: Sliding the calibration back: {0:.1f} cm to go
guard_launch_with_steamvr_desc: SteamVR starts this overlay together with itself. Same switch as the startup overlay apps in the SteamVR settings.
live_intro: What the guard and the solver see right now. Hover a graph, or the info icon next to its title, to see what it shows and how to read it.
live_help_pause: Freezes all graphs at this moment. While paused you can drag to pan and scroll to zoom; every time graph moves along. Recording goes on in the background.
live_paused_hint: Paused at {0}. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom; all graphs move together.
live_no_data: No live data yet. The graphs fill as soon as SteamVR runs and a calibration with a head tracker is active.
live_no_devices: No tracked devices in this window.
live_help_tile_error: How far the head tracker is from where the headset says it should be: now, and the highest value in the last 10 seconds. Under {0} cm is healthy (green); from {1} cm on the guard gets suspicious (red).
live_help_tile_guard: The guard's verdict on the head tracker and how long it has lasted. TRUSTED: all consistent. SUSPECT: it just jumped, the guard waits half a second. UNTRUSTED: the jump stayed. RECOVERING: back in place, waiting for one solve that agrees. The last line says whether the guard holds the calibration (only when hold is on).
live_help_tile_cal: When the solver last changed the calibration, and how many of its attempts in the last 5 minutes were applied or rejected, with the most common reason. Many rejections are normal while you hold still.
live_help_tile_shifts: How often all lighthouse devices moved together this session (the base stations re-solved their positions), and how big the last shift was. These shifts are corrected automatically.
live_help_error:
What it shows: the distance between the head tracker and where the headset plus the learned offset says it should be, over time. Lines at {0} cm (healthy) and {1} cm (the guard gets suspicious). The background turns yellow, red or blue while the guard does not trust the head tracker. Ticks: green = solve applied, orange = universe shift, teal = headset re-center, purple = marker.

How to read it: flat and low means the calibration is good. A short spike is a tracker glitch. A slow climb is drift. A level that drops right after a green tick means the solver fixed it.
live_bullseye_now: now: forward {0} cm, right {1} cm, up {2} cm ({3} cm in total)
live_bullseye_at_back: {0} cm right, {1} cm up: {2} cm from the centre
live_bullseye_at_top: {0} cm right, {1} cm forward: {2} cm from the centre
live_bullseye_at_side: {0} cm forward, {1} cm up: {2} cm from the centre
live_help_bullseye:
What it shows: where the head tracker is compared to where it should be (the centre of each view), in three views on the same scale. From above: right and forward. From the side: forward and up. From behind: right and up, as if you looked over your own shoulder. Directions follow your head: forward is where you face. Newer dots are brighter, the big dot is now. Rings at {0} and {1} cm.

How to read it: a tight cloud in the centre of all three is good. A cloud off-centre is a constant offset, and the views tell you which way (for example below the centre in the side and back views: the head tracker sits lower than the calibration expects). Small offsets (under {0} cm) fade within about ten seconds, because the guard keeps learning how the tracker sits on your head, so a cloud that stays off-centre is a sudden or large offset. A smear that only appears while you turn your head is lag, not a wrong calibration.
live_direction_values: forward {0} cm, right {1} cm, up {2} cm
live_help_direction:
What it shows: the same error split into forward, right and up, relative to where your head faces, over time.

How to read it: the line that leaves zero tells the direction of the problem. Away from zero and steady is an offset. Swinging with your head turns is lag. All three jumping at once is a glitch.
live_cal_values: applied vs now: x {0} cm, y {1} cm, z {2} cm, turn {3} deg
live_help_cal:
What it shows: the applied calibration over time (lines), relative to its value at the right edge: x, y, z in cm and the turn in degrees (right axis). Dots are what each solve proposed: filled = applied, hollow = rejected. Hover a dot for the details.

How to read it: a step in the lines is an applied change. Dots far from the lines that keep getting rejected mean the solver sees something different but does not trust it. Lines that step back and forth mean the solver is hunting.
live_help_glitch:
What it shows: for each device, how far it moved in each frame beyond what its own reported speed explains. The red line is the guard's jump limit.

How to read it: normal movement stays near zero, even when fast. A spike over the line is what the guard calls a jump. A device that keeps hovering near the line is a noisy tracker (battery, line of sight, base station). Click a name in the legend to hide it. Hip and foot are guessed from the tracker's height.
live_help_states:
What it shows: the guard's verdict per device over time. Pale green = trusted, yellow = suspicious, red = not trusted, blue = recovering, grey = not tracking.

How to read it: colour in one row is a problem with that device. Colour in every row at the same moment is a room-wide problem (base station, universe shift).
live_help_rms:
What it shows: for every solve attempt, how well the new solution fits its samples (dots, coloured by what happened to it), and how well the current calibration fits the same samples (line). Lower is better.

How to read it: the solver applies a new solution only when its dot is below the line. A rising line means the current calibration fits worse and worse. Dots far above the line mean the samples disagree (a glitch, or too little movement).
live_help_axis:
What it shows: how well the movement in each solve's samples pins down the rotation (higher is better, log scale). Below the red line the solve is rejected; the program calls that 'axis variance too high'.

How to read it: dots under the line mean you have not turned and moved in enough different directions yet. Look around and move a little, and they rise.
live_solve_rms: error: new {0} mm, current calibration {1} mm
live_solves_none: No solve attempts in this window.
guard_note_hint: A few words, e.g. hip jumped 20 cm when I sat down
guard_hotkey_raise: Bring the window forward for a note
guard_hotkey_raise_desc: After the hotkey this window comes to the front with the cursor in the note field. Enter saves and gives the focus back, Esc skips.
guard_recorder_status: Recording SteamVR session {0}. Records lost so far: {1}.
guard_keep_all_desc: Chunks leaving the live window move to blackbox/sessions instead of being deleted: one folder per SteamVR session, NTFS-compressed (about 0.5 GB per hour of play). Nothing in the archive is ever deleted automatically.
guard_archive_summary_cap: Archive: {0} sessions, {1} GB on disk (cap {2} GB).
guard_archive_cap_reached: Archive cap reached: chunks leaving the live window are deleted again. Raise recorder.archive_max_gb in guard.json to keep archiving.
guard_mark_event_desc: Saves the last minutes of pose data plus the next minutes into an event folder. Press it (or the hotkey) whenever a tracker misbehaves.
guard_last_marker_none: No marker set in this session yet.
guard_markers_session: Markers this session: {0} ({1} automatic of max {2})
guard_ipc_offline: Driver not connected, markers cannot be set.
guard_driver_params_pending: Recorder settings not yet sent to the driver.
guard_hotkey_enabled_desc: Works while a game has focus. The key is polled, so it also fires while the SteamVR dashboard is closed.
guard_hotkey_hint: press the key once to mark
guard_window_desc: How much is kept and how much a marker saves. The live window must be at least as long as the time before a marker.
guard_window_estimate: Estimated disk use of the live window: about {0} MB (10 devices at 250 Hz).
calibration_error_worse_axis_variance_th: Worse axis variance than the current calibration
calibration_error_worse_rms_than_last: Worse fit than the current calibration
calibration_error_lack_of_translational_: Not enough movement in the samples
calibration_error_lack_of_rotational_var: Not enough rotation in the samples
calibration_error_device_untrusted: The head tracker is not trusted right now (Tracker Guard is holding the calibration).
guard_trust_desc: Every tracker is checked against the others each tick. A tracker that jumps while the rest of the body does not is held out of the calibration until it is consistent again.
guard_trust_enabled_desc: Turn off to get the unmodified Space Calibrator behaviour (recording keeps working).
guard_trust_hold: Freeze the calibration while the head tracker is in doubt
guard_trust_hold_desc: Off (observe-only, the default for the first sessions): the guard only shows states, logs and marks events; solver and driver behave exactly like upstream. On: samples from a doubted head tracker are rejected, no solve is applied and the driver holds its correction.
guard_trust_auto_marker: Set a marker on every suspect or untrusted transition
guard_trust_auto_marker_desc: Saves the recording around the event automatically (capped per session).
guard_trust_residual_none: no residual yet (needs a valid continuous calibration)
guard_trust_force_desc: Manual override: every device is trusted again and the next solve is applied (same as holding both triggers).
calibration_error_waiting_for_triggers: Waiting for both triggers to be held before applying (Tracker Guard option).
calibration_error_head_mount_disagrees: The solve would put the head tracker elsewhere on the headset than it has been sitting; ignored (Tracker Guard).
guard_triggers_desc: Hold both controller triggers to recalibrate by hand. This is also the way out of any trust state: it says "everything is tracking, believe the devices again".
guard_triggers_override_desc: Sets a marker, shifts the calibration at once to where the head tracker normally sits on the headset (only shifted, never rotated, no head movement needed) and trusts every device again. The solver then refines it as usual.
guard_triggers_apply_only: Apply continuous updates only while both triggers are held
guard_triggers_apply_only_desc: The 1.5.1 behaviour: the solver keeps running, results are applied only while the hold is active.
guard_triggers_haptics_desc: One pulse when the hold is accepted, a second one when the calibration has been shifted.
guard_triggers_hold_seconds: hold time (how long both triggers must be held)
guard_triggers_input_legacy: Input: legacy controller state (bindings not available)
